summary.text: 家 is built from 宀 above 豕. 宀 contributes a roof or dwelling idea; the lower form’s identity and role are disputed. Early uses for dwelling and household are reported, while the character commonly means house, home, or family today.

formation.text: The construction has competing analyses. The traditional account treats the lower form as an abbreviated 豭 used for sound, alongside 宀 for dwelling. Other accounts read it as a pig beneath a roof and propose a pig enclosure as an original meaning. Matching readings for 家 and 豭 make the phonetic account plausible if 豭 is the relevant element, but do not identify the earliest lower sign or settle the construction.

components.text: 宀 contributes the roof or dwelling idea. It appears as a full component in this graph; no separate earlier form is proposed.

The visible lower form is 豕. Some analyses interpret it as a pig contributing to a roof-and-livestock scene; the traditional account treats it as an abbreviated 豭 sound element. The proposed identity is unsettled, and the claim that an earlier sign 𢑓 changed into 豕 is unverified.

sound_limitation.text: The comparisons support sound compatibility if 豭 is the relevant element; they do not identify the earliest lower sign or provide a reading for proposed sign 𢑓.

sound.text: The modern Mandarin readings match, supporting compatibility if 豭 is the relevant element; this does not assign a reading to visible 豕.
家 and 豭 have the same reconstructed Middle Chinese form in this system, supporting phonetic compatibility if 豭 is the relevant element.
家 and 豭 have the same reconstructed Old Chinese form in this system, supporting phonetic compatibility if 豭 is the relevant element.

history.text: The traditional written analysis treats the lower form as an abbreviation of 豭 serving as a sound element; the regular-script form writes 豕 below 宀. This account does not establish that 豕 developed graphically from 豭.
The proposal that oracle-bone 家 used 𢑓 as its lower sign, later misread or altered into 豕, remains unverified.

uncertainties.text: The lower element’s earliest identity and role remain unsettled: some analyses treat it as a pig contributing to the scene, while the traditional account treats it as an abbreviated sound element. The proposed pig-enclosure original meaning is not established.
Matching readings for 家 and 豭 do not prove that the earliest lower sign was named 豭. No independent ancient pronunciation for the proposed depicted animal or sign is established.

senses.text: Early uses associated with dwelling, including human dwelling in oracle-bone contexts, are reported. A pig-enclosure origin has been proposed but is not established as the earliest meaning.

senses.gloss: ancestral temple, family, royal house or household unit
senses.period: Oracle-bone and bronze uses are reported; sequence unresolved
senses.text: Reported uses include ancestral temple and family, royal house or court, and households counted as 家. Their sequence and relationships are unclear.
家 commonly means house or home, and also family. How these current senses connect to the reported early institutional uses is unclear.

developments.text: Both dwelling and household or institutional uses are reported early, but the evidence does not establish their sequence or a development from one to the other.
The modern senses are established, but their chronology and transition from the early reported uses remain unclear.

limitations.text: Reported early uses do not provide a dated sequence of examined inscriptions, so the chronology of these senses remains unresolved.
The pig-enclosure proposal links a proposed early meaning to human dwelling; the traditional phonetic analysis offers a different account. Neither settles the full history of the word’s meanings.
